name: Machine Incline Chest Press
summary: A seated machine compound press performed on an upward incline to target the upper chest, anterior shoulders, and triceps.

setup: Adjust the seat height so the handles align roughly with your upper chest or clavicle level at the bottom of the movement.
Sit back firmly against the backrest with your feet planted flat on the floor.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, pull your shoulder blades down and back, and brace your core.
steps: Press the handles smoothly upward and forward along the machine's fixed path until your arms are extended without locking your elbows.
Pause briefly at the top while maintaining tension in your upper chest.
Lower the handles under control until you feel a comfortable stretch across your chest, just before the weight stack touches down.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you press the handles away, and inhale as you lower the weight back toward your chest.
cues: Keep your shoulder blades pinned to the pad

common_faults.fault: Setting the seat too high, causing the press to mimic a flat press or putting excessive stress on the shoulders.
common_faults.correction: Lower the seat so the handles align with your upper chest and the pressing angle travels upward.

common_faults.fault: Letting the shoulders roll forward and protract excessively at the top of the press.
common_faults.correction: Keep your upper back pinned against the pad and maintain scapular retraction throughout the rep.

common_faults.fault: Bouncing the weight stack at the bottom of the stroke.
common_faults.correction: Reverse direction smoothly just before the plates touch to maintain continuous muscular tension.

precautions: Avoid using excessive range of motion if you experience anterior shoulder pain.
